title: Store MP webhook and public order-pay inherit the default anonymous throttles — shared Mercado Pago egress IPs may starve legitimate payment notifications
description: StoreMpWebhookView (POST /api/webhooks/store-mp/<slug>/) declares permission_classes=[AllowAny] and authentication_classes=[] but no throttle_classes, so DRF uses DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES = ResilientAnonRateThrottle + ResilientUserRateThrottle (settings.py:75-78). With no authentication, request.user is AnonymousUser: AnonRateThrottle keys throttle_anon_<ident> at 100/day and UserRateThrottle also applies to anonymous requests under throttle_user_<ident> at 1000/day (venv throttling.py:173-202). DaventProject.throttling pins REMOTE_ADDR into the ident (throttling.py:14-27,87-88), but neither default key has a per-view component, so every default-throttled anonymous endpoint shares the same cache key per cache backend/process. The platform MP webhook /api/payments/webhook/ is another AllowAny/default-throttled MP consumer (AdminApp/domains/payments/views/viewset_config.py:66-70), so store and subscription webhook traffic from the same provider egress IPs can share the anon bucket. If MP egress IPs are few and aggregate webhook volume from one IP exceeds the applicable anon cap, later legitimate signed notifications receive HTTP 429 in APIView.initial before HMAC verification, dedup, or StoreMpWebhookQuery run. PublicOrderPayView has the same default-throttle exposure for buyer IPs. Whether starvation occurs depends on MP egress IP distribution/volume, MP retry-on-429 behavior, the active deployment/cache topology, and cache health; none are fully source-visible.
claimed_root_cause: StoreMpWebhookView and PublicOrderPayView omit throttle_classes, so they inherit DRF DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES; for anonymous requests the anon scope enforces 100/day per pinned client IP in a cache key shared by every default-throttled endpoint (with a separate user scope adding a 1000/day IP-keyed bucket), and MP webhook egress IPs may be shared provider infrastructure — aggregate webhook volume from one egress IP can exceed the anon cap and 429 legitimate payment notifications before signature verification.

trace.description: POST /api/webhooks/store-mp/<slug>/ — permission_classes=[AllowAny] (line 110), authentication_classes=[] (line 113), and no throttle_classes on the class, so APIView.throttle_classes falls back to DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES.
DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES = [ResilientAnonRateThrottle, ResilientUserRateThrottle]; DEFAULT_THROTTLE_RATES sets anon=100/day (line 80) and user=1000/day (line 81).

AnonRateThrottle returns None only for authenticated users and otherwise keys throttle_anon_<ident> (177-180); UserRateThrottle does not skip anonymous requests — it keys throttle_user_<ident> by IP for unauthenticated callers (193-202).

Resilient wrappers keep DRF get_cache_key but pin REMOTE_ADDR into the ident via _pinned_ident (14-27); allow_request/wait fail open on cache exceptions (73-85). The resulting keys still have no view/action component.

REDIS_URL selects shared RedisCache for throttling; without it Django locmem is per process. render.yaml declares no REDIS_URL and sets GUNICORN_WORKERS=2, while docker-compose derives REDIS_URL with 3 workers — so whether the anon key is one platform-wide bucket or one bucket per worker is deployment-dependent.

perform_authentication -> check_permissions -> check_throttles run before dispatch to the handler; a failed throttle raises 429 before StoreMpWebhookView.post body-size/store lookup/HMAC/dedup logic (webhook.py:114-183).

evidence.description: class StoreMpWebhookView(APIView): permission_classes=[AllowAny], authentication_classes=[], and no throttle_classes anywhere in the 184-line file.
class PublicOrderPayView(APIView): same pattern — AllowAny, authentication_classes=[], no throttle_classes -> same default anonymous buckets for buyer-initiated MP checkout.
DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES applies ResilientAnonRateThrottle + ResilientUserRateThrottle to every view without explicit throttle_classes; rates are anon 100/day and user 1000/day (lines 79-81).

AnonRateThrottle cache_format throttle_%(scope)s_%(ident)s produces throttle_anon_<ident> for anonymous requests; UserRateThrottle produces throttle_user_<ident> by IP when unauthenticated (193-202). Neither includes the view.
_ResilientThrottleMixin.allow_request/wait fail open on cache exceptions (73-85); get_ident pins REMOTE_ADDR into the DRF ident (87-88, helper at 14-27).
APIView.throttle_classes defaults to api_settings.DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES; get_throttles instantiates them (285-289) and initial calls check_throttles before the handler (419-421).

PaymentConfigs[webhook] uses permissions=[AllowAny] for the platform MP webhook action (viewset.py:140-141) and PaymentViewSet/PaymentBaseViewSet define no throttle_classes, so /api/payments/webhook/ shares the same default anonymous buckets.

The only limit_req_zone is zone=api_token, applied solely to location = /api/token/ (lines 112-115); /api/ and /api/webhooks/* have no nginx limit_req in the compose deploy, and docker/caddy/Caddyfile has no rate-limit directive.
WEBHOOK_DEDUP_SECONDS=600 and cache.add dedup (lines 165-173) run inside post(), i.e. after the throttle check — a 429'd delivery is never dedup-recorded.

REDIS_URL selects shared RedisCache; without it locmem is used per process (409-419). render.yaml:17 comments 'Sin Redis -> caché locmem' and no REDIS_URL is declared, with GUNICORN_WORKERS=2 (render.yaml:185-188); envguard.py:168-174 flags empty REDIS_URL in production as project.E012.

blockers: MP webhook egress IP count/distribution and aggregate daily notification volume across ALL DAVENT store webhooks plus the platform /api/payments/webhook/ consumer are provider/runtime facts not in source; starvation requires the anon cap (100 per rolling day per pinned ident per cache backend/process) to be exceeded by deliveries from one egress IP, including any other anonymous traffic sharing that IP.

MP's retry behavior on HTTP 429 (retry count, backoff schedule, maximum retry age) is provider-side and not documented in the repo — it determines whether throttling merely delays confirmations or permanently drops them after retry exhaustion.

The active deployment is not fully source-visible: docker-compose uses shared Redis and nginx (only /api/token/ has limit_req), while render.yaml declares no REDIS_URL (locmem) and GUNICORN_WORKERS=2; locmem makes the anon cap per worker rather than platform-wide, and any edge/WAF rate limiting in the live path cannot be confirmed from source.
Resilient throttles fail open on cache exceptions — whether the anon/user buckets are enforced depends on cache backend health/availability (locmem always 'works' but is per-process).

validation_plan.local: In a test deployment with a working cache, clear the cache and send 101 POSTs to /api/webhooks/store-mp/<slug>/ from one REMOTE_ADDR/XFF pair (invalid body is fine; the throttle precedes HMAC) and confirm the 101st returns 429; then alternate requests across the store webhook, /api/payments/webhook/, and PublicOrderPayView from the same ident to prove they share throttle_anon_<ident>, and inspect cache keys to confirm the separate throttle_user_<ident> 1000/day bucket also increments. Repeat with cache.get/set raising to confirm fail-open. For locmem multi-worker behavior, run two processes and show each has an independent 100/day bucket.
validation_plan.deployment: Identify the live deployment (compose Redis vs Render locmem) and inspect owner-side production access logs and the MP developer panel for webhook delivery counts per day and source IPs for both /api/webhooks/store-mp/*/ and /api/payments/webhook/; determine whether any single egress IP exceeds the applicable anon cap (100/day under a shared cache, or ~100/day per worker under locmem) and check MP documentation/support for retry-on-429 semantics and horizon. Do not send audit traffic to production; use owner-observed logs/panel data.
